top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength optical lattice clock is a genuinely new regime of control: the trapping light shifts both clock levels equally, so many neutral atoms can be held free of Doppler and recoil broadening. The claim is verified by independent laboratories agreeing near 1e-18, and it has already produced results about nature (millimetre-scale redshift, limits on varying constants, many-body physics in the lattice). The two-name allocation to Katori (concept and first strontium realisation) and Ye (record accuracy and many-body work) is clean, and a citation of invention and development is correctly scoped. The overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes is real but does not cover neutral atoms in a lattice, so an award is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no stated collaboration with Katori or Ye, though as a theorist in atomic many-body physics and a close collaborator of 2023 laureate L'Huillier she works in a neighbouring field.
